newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Christians inaugurate Holy Sepulchre rotunda.
newsitem.headline: Christians inaugurate Holy Sepulchre rotunda.

text.p: Christianity's holiest site, Jerusalem's Church of the Holy Sepulchre, celebrated on Thursday the inauguration of a newly decorated rotunda designed to represent God enveloping the risen Christ, local churches said.

"The event symbolises Christian unity. I hope it will be the beginning of the uniting of the Christian churches in the Holy Land in preparation to celebrate the second millennium of Jesus Christ," a spokesman at the ceremony told Reuters.
The dome, built above the traditional tomb of Jesus Christ, was renovated in 1980, but scaffolding kept the rotunda concealed since then. Renovations began in 1994.

A church statement said the design, made by California artist Era Normart, depicts 12 streams of gold representing the 12 Apostles while three rays of light symbolising the Trinity branch down from each stream.

Light from the dome's central skylight, as well as from concealed artificial sources, enhances the mother-of-pearl background which brightens as it ascends and sparkles with stars, the statement added.
Leaders of Greek Orthodox, Latin and Armenian Churches, who are also the custodians of the Church, presided over the ceremony held at the church inside Jerusalem's Old City.
Members of the cabinet of Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and the Israeli mayor of Jerusalem were among the 200 guests from around the world who attended the ceremony.
The church was built in 1042 on the ruins of the original church built in 335 by Roman Emperor Constantine. In the last 200 years, two major fires and an earthquake damaged the building.
The ceremony spokesman said that American George Doty from New York City donated the funds for the renovations, which cost about $2 million.
